summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update4.json → valid=true). Adversarial coverage check of the two recorded A2 findings against the retained tests, since an existing expectation that fixed target eligibility or the TimeoutNow receiver would have narrowed or refuted them. What the suite actually fixes: LeadershipTransferToServer with an unknown ID must fail with 'cannot find replication state' (raft_test.go:2502-2515); with an unreachable address must fail with 'failed to make TimeoutNow RPC' (2518-2532); with a voting follower — including while writes continue (2433-2486) and in a seven-node cluster (2488-2500) — must succeed and that follower must become leader; a behind-but-reachable voting follower must also succeed (2534-2553, after 1000 commits); and the automatic path in a two-node cluster whose only other voter was demoted must fail with 'cannot find peer' (2636-2654). Decisive gaps: the test named TestRaft_LeadershipTransferIgnoresNonvoters exercises only the automatic LeadershipTransfer(), so it pins pickServer's voter filter and never reaches the explicit target; no test passes a non-voting server as the explicit target; and no test body asserts any receive-side property of TimeoutNow (the only TimeoutNow string in the suite is the unreachable-target error text). Recorded as one Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation with counterevidence and limits — notably that a test name is evidence of intent, not enforcement, and that no execution was performed (tests were read, not run; this run's experiment capacity is exhausted). Net effect on the two prior findings: neither is refuted, the requirement side is stronger because the intent is named by the suite, and the protective side is weaker because the handler that performs the transition has no guard and no test.
